title: [Bug]: Log is full of "failed to start a background worker"
body: My TimescaleDB log is repeatedly filled with warnings that job 3, "Job History Log Retention Policy [3]", failed to start a background worker. Increasing max_worker_processes from 32 to 64 and timescaledb.max_background_workers from 8 through 16 and 32 to 48 did not make the launch failures disappear. This is PostgreSQL 16 using the latest-pg16 TimescaleDB Docker image on Alpine Linux with Zabbix 7. I also use pgBackRest with archive_mode enabled.

symptoms_visible: My TimescaleDB log repeatedly says that job 3, "Job History Log Retention Policy [3]", failed to start a background worker.
The warnings continue even though I increased max_worker_processes to 64 and timescaledb.max_background_workers to 48.
N0.label: N0 background-worker warning flood reported

symptoms_visible: After a fresh server restart, PostgreSQL becomes ready, the TimescaleDB launcher connects, and repeated job 3 background-worker launch warnings begin within a few seconds.
N1.label: N1 warnings reproduced after restart

symptoms_visible: The repeated job 3 background-worker launch warnings are still present.
N2.label: N2 activity count collected

symptoms_visible: The scheduler still cannot start background jobs, and the warning flood continues.
N3.label: N3 runtime worker-slot value measured

symptoms_visible: The log is still producing background-worker launch warnings while the runtime worker-slot total is 4.
N4.label: N4 overriding configuration source found

symptoms_visible: After I removed the max_worker_processes = 4 entry from postgresql.auto.conf and restarted the server, the majority of the background-worker launch failures were gone.
I later saw one separate Telemetry Reporter timeout and exit-code-1 event rather than the previous continuous launch-warning flood.
N_terminal.label: terminal original warning flood resolved

question_patterns: Did you restart PostgreSQL after changing the worker parameters?
Were these settings followed by a full server restart rather than only a configuration reload?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I did a fresh restart after changing the parameters.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, I only reloaded the configuration and have not restarted PostgreSQL.
Yes, I restarted the entire Docker container rather than only the PostgreSQL process.

question_patterns: Can you share the log from a fresh restart, including anything printed by the same PIDs before the warnings?
What appears in the PostgreSQL log immediately before the first failed-worker warning after startup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: From a fresh restart, PostgreSQL reports that it is ready, the TimescaleDB background worker launcher connects to the shared catalogs, and then the failed-to-launch-job-3 warnings start within a few seconds. There is no other error from those PIDs before the warnings in the log I posted.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same PID first prints a library-loading or permission error immediately before every failed-worker warning.

edges.comment: From participant1 c0 and reporter c1, describing the original reporter's Docker/PostgreSQL system: the maintainer requested preceding log events and confirmation of a restart; the reporter supplied a fresh-start log showing the warnings recur immediately.

question_patterns: How many rows do you currently have in pg_stat_activity?
Could you run SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity and report the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran select count(*) from pg_stat_activity; it is 42 most of the time and sometimes 43.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It stays at 3 or 4 rows even while the warning is occurring.
It fluctuates between 41 and 44 instead of 42 and 43.

edges.comment: From participant1 c3 and reporter c4 on the original reporter's server: the maintainer requested an SQL-visible process count, and the reporter returned the raw count without claiming how it mapped to worker slots.

question_patterns: Can you attach a debugger and capture what RegisterDynamicBackgroundWorker returns when the warning occurs?
If you can use gdb, what does the worker-registration call return and what caller appears in the backtrace?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached gdb to PID 35 and broke on RegisterDynamicBackgroundWorker. The backtrace goes through ts_bgw_start_worker for "Telemetry Reporter [1]", and after finishing the calls the BackgroundWorkerHandle value is 0x0.

question_patterns: Using the debugger command for the first field of BackgroundWorkerData, what integer value do you get?
Can you inspect the runtime total worker-slot value in BackgroundWorkerData and paste the raw result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran `(gdb) print *(int*) BackgroundWorkerData` and got `$2 = 4`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debugger prints 64 for that value.

edges.comment: From participant1 c5/c11 and reporter c10/c13 on the reporter's server. These are debugger measurements: the reporter supplied the raw stack, NULL handle, and integer value 4; the conclusion that this contradicts the intended max_worker_processes setting remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you check every PostgreSQL configuration source for another max_worker_processes entry?
Please verify whether postgresql.conf or any automatically generated configuration file contains a second value for max_worker_processes.
Are you editing the configuration file that supplies the active setting, and is another configuration source overriding it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found a postgresql.auto.conf generated via psql and pgtune. It contains `max_worker_processes = '4'`; pgtune had used my four-CPU count for that value.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no second entry anywhere, and every configuration source contains max_worker_processes = 64.
The overriding entry is in an included configuration file rather than postgresql.auto.conf, but it also sets the value to 4.
The configuration files use different whitespace around the equals sign.

edges.comment: From participant1 c15-c17 and reporter c16/c18 on the reporter's system. After the debugger showed only four runtime slots, the maintainer asked the reporter to check duplicate entries, the correct file, and restart handling; the reporter found the pgtune-generated value in postgresql.auto.conf.

solution.intent: Correct the effective PostgreSQL worker setting by removing or replacing the max_worker_processes = 4 override in postgresql.auto.conf, restart PostgreSQL so the intended value takes effect, and verify that the repeated TimescaleDB launch warnings stop.
solution.concrete_example: The runtime slot count is 4 because postgresql.auto.conf overrides the value written in postgresql.conf. Remove or correct that conflicting max_worker_processes entry, restart the Dockerized PostgreSQL server, then check the log and runtime setting again. The reporter removed the pgtune-generated `max_worker_processes = '4'` line and reported that the majority of the launch failures disappeared.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter's raw debugger result is only `BackgroundWorkerData` equal to 4. Combining that measurement with the later discovery of `max_worker_processes = '4'` in postgresql.auto.conf establishes the accepted diagnosis: PostgreSQL configuration precedence kept the effective worker-slot limit at four, so editing postgresql.conf to 64 had no effect.

edges.comment: Resolution from reporter c18 and participant1 c19-c20 on the original reporter's deployment. The reporter removed the pgtune-generated override, restarted, and observed that the majority of the background-worker failures were gone. The isolated Telemetry Reporter timeout subsequently shown is retained as a separate observed event and is not substituted for the resolved warning-flood root cause.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: postgresql.auto.conf contained a pgtune-generated max_worker_processes = 4 setting that overrode the intended value in postgresql.conf, leaving only four runtime background-worker slots and causing slot exhaustion.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence, especially the fresh-restart reproduction, the raw debugger value of four total slots, and the conflicting postgresql.auto.conf entry.

Must recommend removing or correcting the conflicting automatic configuration entry and fully restarting PostgreSQL; merely increasing values in postgresql.conf or timescaledb.max_background_workers while the override remains is insufficient and was already ineffective.

Must not attribute the final root cause to the four-CPU hardware limit, pgBackRest, archive_mode, or a leaking WAL archiver process; the final thread diagnosis was configuration precedence, not a CPU-bound slot count or archiver leak.

Must ask the reporter to verify after restart that the repeated background-worker launch-warning flood has stopped before declaring the original issue resolved; an isolated later Telemetry Reporter timeout may be treated separately.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically advanced database operator comfortable with Docker, PostgreSQL configuration, SQL diagnostics, verbose logging, and attaching gdb to a running backend, but initially unaware that an automatically generated PostgreSQL configuration file was overriding the manually edited value.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, evidence-driven, and concise; quotes questions before answering, pastes raw logs and debugger output, tests hypotheses independently, and challenges explanations that conflict with observations.
